notes: CalibForge owns this task. It carries a deliberate polyglot family of six - Python+C prime (software-engineering_20260415_123352_017, the one flagged in the brief), Python+C prime factorisation, bash+C primality, C+shell base64, a self-compiling shell/C file, and a three-way python3/bash/gcc Fibonacci polyglot (software-engineering_20260617_210354_017) that is the same problem as this TB2.1 task with one extra language. All six are graded `strong` and their tests really invoke each toolchain and compare, so this is the clearest case in my five tasks of a new corpus beating everything in the v1 pool outright. Terminal-Lego-15k contributes exactly one genuine polyglot (task_00979, bat+bash) plus preprocessor and Fibonacci exercises. Outside those two, nobody in the pool has a single-source-two-grammars task: TMax's many 'polyglot' hits are multi-language build systems, and Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld offer quines and MetaCall cross-runtime calls, which share the self-reference and two-languages ideas but not the parser trick. SWE-Rebench is unexpectedly useful at rank 1-3 via pyccel (Python-to-C translation semantics) and useless below that; SWE-Smith could not field 10 defensible candidates and ranks 4-10 are 1s and 2s.
